newsitem.title: CANADA: South Manitoba to be cool, clear through Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: South Manitoba to be cool, clear through Tuesday.

text.p: Southern Manitoba's Red River Valley was forecast to see cool but clear weather through Tuesday, Environment Canada said.
Manitoba's Red River Valley was forecast to see mainly sunny skies Friday with highs of eight to 11 degrees Celsius.
Normal lows at this time of year are -2 Celsius and highs are +10 Celsius.
As much as 250,000 acres of farmland were forecast to flood later this month when Manitoba's Red River crests, officials said.
Grains and oilseeds are grown in the Canadian Red River Valley.
The area should see sunny skies Saturday with highs of seven degrees C with light northerly winds, Environment Canada said.

Mainly sunny skies were forecast for Sunday with highs of four to eight degrees C. Monday should be sunny also with highs of four to eight. Tuesday should see mainly sunny skies, again with highs of four to eight C.
Low temperatures into Tuesday were forecast to drop to -4 C.
Winnipeg saw 211.4 cm (83 inches) of snow since October 1 compared with average snowfall totals in that period of 108.8 cm (43 inches), Environment Canada said.
